title: Mac Dictation Not Working? How to Fix It (2026)
summary: Ten checks from Apple's own guide for Mac dictation that will not start, stops mid-sentence, or hears you wrong.
body_markdown:
You press the key, the cursor does not pulse, and nothing you say shows up. Or dictation starts, types half a sentence, and quits. Mac dictation is reliable once it is set up, but it depends on a stack of small settings (the switch, the shortcut, the language, the microphone, a connection) and any one of them can quietly break it. This guide works through them in the order that resolves the most cases, using Apple's own Mac User Guide for macOS 27 as it reads at the time of writing. The same System Settings layout applies back to macOS Ventura; on older versions the app is called System Preferences.


**The short answer:** open System Settings, click Keyboard, and confirm Dictation is on. Then check that you are pressing the shortcut shown in the Shortcut menu, that Voice Control is off under Accessibility, that the right microphone is selected as the Microphone source with its input level up, and that your language is in the Dictation languages list. If dictation stops on its own, it heard no speech for 30 seconds.


## Why Mac dictation stops working


Dictation is not an app. It is a system feature that listens through whichever microphone macOS has chosen, sends or processes your speech depending on your Mac and language, and types the result into whatever has keyboard focus. So when it fails, the cause is almost always one of five things: it was switched off (often after a macOS update or a settings reset), the shortcut you are pressing is not the one that is configured, another voice feature has taken over the microphone, the microphone itself is wrong or muted, or the language and connection it needs are missing. The fixes below take those in turn. If you have never set dictation up on this Mac, start with our guide to[how to use dictation on a Mac](https://aquavoice.com/blog/how-to-use-dictation-on-mac) and come back here if something still fails.


## 1. Confirm Dictation is on, then switch it off and on again


Apple's first instruction is the obvious one, and it catches more cases than you would think.


1. Choose the Apple menu, then **System Settings** .
2. Click **Keyboard** in the sidebar (scroll down if you do not see it).
3. Go to the **Dictation** section and check the switch.


If it is off, turn it on and click **Enable** . If your Mac asks whether you want to improve Siri and Dictation, choose Share Audio Recordings or Not Now; either answer leaves dictation working, and you can change it later under Privacy & Security, in Analytics & Improvements.


If the switch is already on, turn it off, wait a few seconds, and turn it back on. This re-enables the feature cleanly and is the quickest first step after an update.


**If the Dictation section is missing or greyed out,** the feature is being restricted rather than broken. On a personal Mac, open **Screen Time** in System Settings and look under **Content & Privacy Restrictions** , where Apple's Screen Time controls can block Siri and other features; clear anything that was set there and check Keyboard settings again. On a work or school Mac, a configuration profile from your IT team can restrict dictation, in which case only they can turn it back on.


## 2. Check the shortcut you are pressing


The most common "dictation is broken" report is really a shortcut mismatch. There are three ways to start dictation, and only one of them has to work for you to know the feature itself is fine.


- **The Microphone key.** On recent Mac keyboards it sits in the function row. Apple's note matters here: **press and release** the Microphone key to start dictation; **press and hold** it and you get Siri instead. If you hold it out of habit, dictation never starts.
- **The Dictation keyboard shortcut.** In System Settings, under Keyboard, open the **Shortcut** pop-up menu in the Dictation section and read what is selected. If it says Press Fn (Function) Key Twice, a single press or a press of the Globe key on its own will not do it. Apple also notes that choosing a Dictation shortcut can change the "Press fn key to" or "Press Globe key to" option in Keyboard settings automatically, so if you later set that option to Change Input Source or Show Emoji & Symbols, the double-press may stop starting dictation. Set it back, or choose **Customize** in the Shortcut menu and press a combination nothing else uses (Apple's example is Option-Z).
- **The Edit menu.** In most apps, choose **Edit** , then **Start Dictation** . This is the test to run first: if the menu item starts dictation and the key does not, the feature works and the shortcut is the problem.


While you are in that section, confirm the cursor actually highlights and pulses (or you hear the tone) when dictation starts. If it does, dictation is listening and the remaining fixes are about what it hears.


## 3. Turn off Voice Control


macOS has two voice features, and they do not run side by side. Apple states it plainly in the Voice Control guide: when Voice Control is on, you dictate through Voice Control, and standard Dictation is not available. If your shortcut suddenly does nothing, or you see a microphone overlay you do not recognize, this is a likely cause.


Open System Settings, click **Accessibility** , click **Voice Control** , and turn it off. Then try your Dictation shortcut again. (If you want Voice Control for hands-free use of the whole Mac, keep it on and say "Dictation mode" to enter text; the two features just cannot both own the microphone.)


## 4. Fix the microphone


Apple's troubleshooting page spends most of its words here, because a mic that is wrong, quiet, or blocked produces exactly the symptom people report: the cursor pulses, you speak, and nothing appears.


1. **Pick the right source.** In System Settings, under Keyboard, in the Dictation section, open the pop-up menu next to **Microphone source** . Automatic lets your Mac choose the device you are most likely to use; if you have a headset or an external microphone, select it by name. If you unplugged a USB mic that was selected here, switch back to the built-in one.
2. **Raise the input level.** Open **Sound** in System Settings, click **Input** , select the microphone, and watch the level meter while you talk. If it barely moves, drag the input volume up. Apple's guidance is to speak clearly at a volume that is neither too quiet nor too loud, positioned as you would normally sit at your Mac.
3. **Unblock it.** Make sure nothing covers the built-in microphone, including clothing, a sleeve, or your hand, and check your Mac's getting-started guide if you are not sure where the mic is. Desktop Macs without a built-in microphone need an external one connected and selected before dictation can hear anything.
4. **Cut the noise.** In a noisy room, or one with a lot of echo, Apple suggests a headset microphone. Background noise is a leading cause of dictation that runs but types the wrong words.


One thing that is not the fix: the **Microphone** list under **Privacy & Security** . That list controls which apps may record audio themselves. Apple's Dictation is a system feature rather than an app, so you will not find it there, and toggling apps on that screen does not change whether built-in dictation can hear you. It does matter for third-party dictation apps, which we come back to below.


## 5. Check the language and region


Dictation listens for the language you have set, and Apple's second troubleshooting item is to choose the correct language and region. In System Settings, under Keyboard, in the Dictation section, click **Edit** next to **Languages** and confirm the language you speak is selected with the right region. If you dictate in more than one language, add each one; you can switch while dictating by clicking the language label next to the cursor, or by pressing the Globe key and choosing from the list.


If your language is already selected and dictation still types nothing, deselect it, close the sheet, then select it again and retry. Dictation is not available in every language or region, and features vary by language; Apple's macOS Feature Availability page lists which languages you can dictate in.


## 6. Check your internet connection (and whether you need one)


Depending on your Mac and your language, dictation either processes your speech on the device or sends it to Apple's servers. Apple tells you which applies to you: with Dictation enabled, open System Settings, click Keyboard, and read the text below the Dictation switch. If it says your voice input for general text dictation is processed on your device, dictation works offline. If it does not say that, you need a connection, and a Mac that is on Wi-Fi but not actually online (a captive portal at a hotel, a VPN that has dropped) will start dictation and then type nothing.


To check, open **Network** in System Settings and confirm you are connected. Then load a web page.


## 7. Dictation works in one app but not another


If dictation types fine in Notes but not in another app, the feature is healthy and the problem is where the text is going. Dictation inserts text at the insertion point, so click directly into the field you want to fill before you press the shortcut; if nothing on screen has keyboard focus, your words have nowhere to land. Some fields, such as password fields, may not accept dictation at all. And remember that dictating into a search box is handled differently from general text dictation, which is why Apple's privacy note separates the two.


If a specific third-party app has its own voice input feature that fails, that is where the Privacy & Security microphone list from fix 4 comes in: open it and make sure that app is allowed to use the microphone.


## 8. Restart, update, and try safe mode


When the settings are all correct and dictation still refuses to start, fall back to the general fixes.


1. **Restart the Mac.** Choose the Apple menu, then Restart. A restart clears whatever state the speech services were stuck in.
2. **Update macOS.** Open System Settings, click General, then Software Update, and install anything waiting. Dictation bugs are fixed in point releases, and an interrupted update is a common reason a feature disappears.
3. **Start up in safe mode.** Apple's guide explains that safe mode helps you tell whether a problem comes from software that loads at startup. On a Mac with Apple silicon, shut down, press and hold the power button until "Loading startup options" appears, select your startup disk, then hold Shift and click Continue in Safe Mode. On an Intel Mac, restart and hold Shift until the login window appears. You should see "Safe Boot" in the menu bar. If dictation works in safe mode, a login item or a third-party audio or keyboard utility is interfering; restart normally and remove them one at a time.
4. **Test in a new user account.** Add a user under Users & Groups, log in as that user, and try dictation. If it works there, the fault is in your account's settings rather than macOS, and re-enabling dictation, re-adding your language, and resetting the shortcut from a clean state usually clears it.


## 9. Dictation keeps stopping mid-sentence


This is the other half of the search, and it usually is not a fault. Apple's rules are specific:


- You can dictate text of **any length** without a timeout while you are speaking.
- Dictation **stops automatically when no speech is detected for 30 seconds.** Pause to think for half a minute and the session ends.
- Dictation also stops when you press **Escape** , the **Microphone key** , or your **Dictation shortcut** . If your shortcut is a key you also use for something else, you may be stopping it by accident.
- On a Mac with **Apple silicon** , you can keep typing while you dictate: the cursor stops pulsing while you type and resumes when you stop. Apple's guide describes that behavior for Apple silicon specifically and does not promise it on Intel Macs, so if dictation ends when you touch the keyboard on an older machine, press the shortcut and carry on.


If it stops within a few seconds of starting and types nothing, go back to fix 4 (the mic is not picking you up, so the 30-second silence rule is firing) and fix 6 (the connection dropped).


## 10. Dictation runs but gets the words wrong


Dictation that is working, just badly, is worth a separate minute. Ambiguous words are underlined in blue; click one and pick the alternative, or retype it. If punctuation is appearing where you did not want it, Auto-punctuation is on in the Dictation settings and can be turned off, after which you speak the marks yourself ("comma," "new paragraph"). Reduce background noise, move closer to the mic, and check the language and region once more: dictation set to the wrong English region will still work, just with more mistakes. Beyond that, accuracy on names, jargon, and technical terms is a limit of the feature rather than a setting, since standard Dictation has no vocabulary you can edit.

## FAQ


### Why is dictation not working on my Mac?


Most often because Dictation is switched off under System Settings, Keyboard, or because the shortcut you are pressing is not the one selected in the Shortcut menu (press and release the Microphone key; holding it opens Siri). After that, check that Voice Control is off under Accessibility, that the right microphone is selected as the Microphone source with its input level up, and that your language is selected in the Dictation languages list.


### Why does my Mac dictation keep stopping?


Apple's dictation stops automatically when it detects no speech for 30 seconds, and it also stops when you press Escape, the Microphone key, or your Dictation shortcut. While you are speaking there is no time limit. If it stops within seconds and types nothing, the microphone is not picking you up or, on a Mac that does not process dictation on device, the internet connection dropped.


### Does Mac dictation need an internet connection?


It depends on your Mac and language. With Dictation enabled, read the text under the Dictation switch in Keyboard settings: it says whether your general text dictation is processed on your device. If it is not, dictation needs a connection. Apple's macOS Feature Availability page lists the supported dictation languages.


### How do I reset dictation on a Mac?


There is no single reset button. Turn Dictation off and back on in Keyboard settings, re-select your language under Languages, set the Shortcut again, and restart the Mac. If it still fails, start up in safe mode or test in a new user account to find out whether a login item or your account settings are the cause.
